items.sentence: The coach insisted that Marco ___ at practice by six.
items.why: After 'insisted that', use the base form 'be' for a demand.

items.sentence: If I ___ you, I would save my load for emergencies.
items.why: For an imagined situation, 'If I were' is the standard form, not 'was'.

items.sentence: I wish Tita Nena ___ here to see the fiesta parade.
items.why: After 'wish' for something not true now, use 'were' with every subject.

items.sentence: It is important that each student ___ the exam on time.
items.why: After 'It is important that', use the base form 'finish' without -s.

items.sentence: Kuya Ron suggested that Lyka ___ the jeepney instead of a tricycle.
items.why: After 'suggested that', use the base form 'take' even with a singular subject.

items.sentence: The principal demanded that every section ___ its classroom before dismissal.
items.why: After 'demanded that', the verb stays in its base form 'clean'.

items.sentence: If Jom ___ the captain, he would let everyone play.
items.why: For an unreal 'if' situation, use 'were' even with 'he' or 'she'.

items.sentence: Bea wishes her father ___ not working abroad this Christmas.
items.why: After 'wishes' about something not true now, use 'were' for any subject.

items.sentence: Neither the players nor the coach ___ ready for the finals.
items.why: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearest subject, 'the coach', so use 'is'.

items.sentence: Either Lyka or her cousins ___ bringing the merienda tomorrow.
items.why: With 'either...or', the verb matches the nearest subject, 'cousins', so use 'are'.

items.sentence: A number of students ___ absent because of the typhoon.
items.why: 'A number of' means 'many', so it takes a plural verb like 'are'.

items.sentence: The number of jeepneys on our route ___ dropped since the strike.
items.why: 'The number of' is a single amount, so it takes a singular verb like 'has'.

items.sentence: There ___ several sari-sari stores near the barangay hall.
items.why: After 'there', the verb matches the real subject, 'several stores', which is plural.

items.sentence: Five kilometers ___ a long walk when the tricycles are not running.
items.why: A distance treated as one amount takes a singular verb, so use 'is'.

items.sentence: Two hundred pesos ___ enough load for the whole week.
items.why: An amount of money counted as one sum is singular, so use 'is'.

items.sentence: Playing online games all night ___ a bad idea before exams.
items.why: A gerund subject like 'playing' is singular, so the verb is 'is'.

items.sentence: Marco enjoys running, swimming, and ___ basketball on weekends.
items.why: Items in a list must match in form, so use 'playing' like 'running' and 'swimming'.

items.sentence: Lyka is not only smart but also ___ to her classmates.
items.why: With 'not only...but also', both parts must match, so use the adjective 'kind' like 'smart'.

items.sentence: After class, we either review our notes or ___ basketball at the court.
items.why: With 'either...or', both verbs must match, so use 'play' like 'review'.

items.sentence: The barangay captain promised to fix the road, clean the canal, and ___ new streetlights.
items.why: Verbs in a list must share one form, so use 'install' like 'fix' and 'clean'.

items.sentence: Jom wants to finish his homework, to help his mother, and ___ early.
items.why: The list uses 'to' forms, so the last item must also be 'to sleep'.

items.sentence: Bea would rather save her allowance than ___ it on load.
items.why: After 'would rather...than', both verbs take the base form, so use 'spend' like 'save'.

items.sentence: The new teacher is patient, funny, and ___ with every student.
items.why: A list of adjectives must stay adjectives, so use 'fair' like 'patient' and 'funny'.

items.sentence: Whether you ride the jeepney or ___ to school, be there by seven.
items.why: With 'whether...or', both verbs must match, so use 'walk' like 'ride'.

items.sentence: If Marco had studied last night, he ___ passing the exam now.
items.why: A past 'if' with a present result uses 'would be', not 'would have been'.

items.sentence: ___ I known about the typhoon, I would have stayed home.
items.why: 'Had I known' is the inverted form of 'If I had known'.

items.sentence: Lyka will not get her phone back ___ she finishes her homework.
items.why: 'Unless' means 'if not', so she gets the phone only after finishing.

items.sentence: You can borrow my notes ___ you return them before Friday.
items.why: 'As long as' sets a condition that must be met, like 'only if'.

items.sentence: Bring an umbrella ___ it rains during the fiesta parade.
items.why: 'In case' means you prepare for something that might happen.

items.sentence: If Jom ___ the jeepney earlier, he would not be late now.
items.why: A past condition with a present result uses 'had' plus the past participle.

items.sentence: ___ the tricycle fare lower, more students would ride to school.
items.why: 'Were the fare lower' is the inverted form of 'If the fare were lower'.

items.sentence: If I were taller, I ___ joined the varsity team last year.
items.why: A present condition with a past result uses 'would have' plus the past participle.

items.sentence: Bea ___ studied harder; she failed the quiz.
items.why: 'Should have' plus the past participle shows a past action that was the right thing but did not happen.

items.sentence: Kuya Ron's shoes are wet, so it ___ rained while he was walking home.
items.why: 'Must have' plus the past participle shows a strong guess about the past.

items.sentence: Marco ___ scored if he had passed the ball earlier.
items.why: 'Could have' plus the past participle shows a past chance that was missed.

items.sentence: Lyka ___ left her charger at school; it is not in her bag.
items.why: 'Might have' plus the past participle shows a possible past action.

items.sentence: You ___ bring food tomorrow; the fiesta hosts will feed everyone.
items.why: 'Need not' means it is not necessary, and it never takes -s.

items.sentence: Students ___ to greet the teacher when she enters the room.
items.why: 'Ought' is the only modal followed by 'to'; 'should' and 'must' take the bare verb.

items.sentence: Jom ___ called from the mall, but his phone had no load.
items.why: 'Could have' plus the past participle shows something possible in the past that did not happen.

items.sentence: We ___ to help Tita Nena carry the sacks of rice.
items.why: 'Ought to' means 'should'; the other modals never take 'to'.
